This document is confidential and contains proprietary information belonging to NovoPharm Clinical. It may not be used, disclosed, or reproduced without prior written consent. The current version in use at all participating sites is Protocol MOC-221-Rev3.

1. BACKGROUND AND RATIONALE

Pancreatic adenocarcinoma remains a disease with significant unmet medical need. Despite advances in systemic therapy, the five-year survival rate for subjects with locally advanced or metastatic disease remains below 10%. The standard of care, gemcitabine-based regimens, offers modest survival benefit but is associated with substantial toxicity. There is therefore a pressing need for novel therapeutic approaches that can improve outcomes without unacceptable adverse effects.

MOC-221 is a selective small molecule inhibitor targeting the MAPK signalling pathway downstream of KRAS mutations. Preclinical studies demonstrated synergistic anti-tumour activity when MOC-221 was combined with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel in xenograft models. The current Phase II study is designed to evaluate this combination in a larger cohort of subjects with pancreatic adenocarcinoma who have not received prior systemic therapy for advanced disease.

2. STUDY OBJECTIVES

2.1 Primary Objective

To evaluate the anti-tumour activity of MOC-221 in combination with standard-of-care chemotherapy as measured by progression-free survival (PFS) per RECIST v1.1 as assessed by investigator review.

2.2 Secondary Objectives

- To characterise the safety and tolerability profile of MOC-221 when administered with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel
- To estimate overall survival (OS)
- To evaluate objective response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DoR)
- To assess pharmacokinetic parameters of MOC-221 when given in combination
- To evaluate changes in quality of life using the EORTC QLQ-C30 instrument

MOC-221 protocol_version_in_use Protocol MOC-221-Rev3. Record status: current.

2.3 Exploratory Objectives

- To investigate the relationship between tumour KRAS mutation status and clinical activity
- To evaluate potential predictive biomarkers in archival tumour tissue
- To assess immunogenicity of MOC-221

3. STUDY DESIGN

This is a Phase II, open-label, single-arm, multi-centre study. A total of approximately 75 subjects will be enrolled across approximately 15 sites in Asia-Pacific, including Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, and Australia.

Subjects will receive MOC-221 at a dose of 300 mg orally twice daily continuously in 28-day cycles. In addition, subjects will receive gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² intravenously on Days 1, 8, and 15 of each cycle and nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m² intravenously on Days 1, 8, and 15 of each cycle.

Treatment will continue until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal of consent, or a maximum of 12 cycles of chemotherapy, whichever occurs first. Subjects who complete 12 cycles of chemotherapy and derive clinical benefit may receive MOC-221 monotherapy until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

The study will utilise a Simon two-stage design. An interim analysis will be conducted after the first 25 subjects have been followed for at least 16 weeks. If fewer than 8 subjects are progression-free at that timepoint, enrolment will be halted for futility. Otherwise, the study will continue to full enrolment.

4. SUBJECT SELECTION

4.1 Inclusion Criteria

Subjects must satisfy all of the following criteria to be eligible for the study:
4.1.5 Subjects must have adequate haematological, hepatic, and renal function as defined below:
- Absolute neutrophil count ≥ 1.5 × 10⁹/L
- Haemoglobin ≥ 9.0 g/dL
- Platelet count ≥ 100 × 10⁹/L
- Total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 × upper limit of normal (ULN)
- AST and ALT ≤ 3.0 × ULN (≤ 5.0 × ULN if liver metastases are present)
- Serum creatinine ≤ 1.5 × ULN or calculated creatinine clearance ≥ 50 mL/min

4.1.6 Subjects must have an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 or 1.

4.1.7 Subjects must have archival tumour tissue available for KRAS mutation status testing, or consent to a fresh biopsy at screening.

4.1.8 Subjects must be willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures.

**4.2 Exclusion Criteria**

Subjects who meet any of the following criteria are not eligible for the study:

4.2.1 Prior systemic therapy for metastatic PDAC. Prior adjuvant therapy is permitted if completed at least 6 months prior to diagnosis of metastatic disease.

4.2.2 Known active central nervous system metastases.

4.2.3 Clinically significant cardiovascular disease, including myocardial infarction within 6 months, unstable angina, New York Heart Association Class III or IV congestive heart failure, or QTc interval > 470 ms on screening ECG.

4.2.4 Known history of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection, active hepatitis B or hepatitis C infection.

4.2.5 Major surgical procedure within 28 days prior to first dose of study treatment.

4.2.6 Known hypersensitivity to any component of MOC-221, gemcitabine, or nab-paclitaxel.

4.2.7 Pregnant or breastfeeding women. Women of childbearing potential must have a negative serum pregnancy test at screening and agree to use highly effective contraception during the study and for 6 months after the last dose of study treatment.

The enrollment target for MOC-221 is 80 patients. Record status: current.

4.2.8 Any other condition that, in the opinion of the investigator, would compromise the safety of the subject or interfere with the interpretation of study results.

**5. STUDY TREATMENT**

**5.1 Dosing Schedule**

Subjects will receive the following treatment regimens in 28-day cycles:

| Drug | Dose | Route | Schedule |
|------|------|-------|----------|
| MOC-221 | 300 mg | Oral | Twice daily, Days 1–28 continuously |
| Gemcitabine | 1000 mg/m² | IV | Days 1, 8, 15 |
| Nab-paclitaxel | 125 mg/m² | IV | Days 1, 8, 15 |

MOC-221 should be taken with food at approximately the same time each morning and evening. If a dose is missed, the subject should not make up the dose; the next scheduled dose should be taken at the regular time.

**5.2 Dose Modifications**

Dose modifications for gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel will follow standard guidelines for haematological and non-haematological toxicities. MOC-221 dose modifications are as follows:

- Grade 2 non-haematological toxicity (excluding alopecia): hold MOC-221 until resolution to ≤ Grade 1, then resume at same dose.
- Grade 3 non-haematological toxicity: hold MOC-221 until resolution to ≤ Grade 1, then resume at reduced dose of 200 mg twice daily.
- Grade 4 toxicity: discontinue MOC-221 permanently.

**5.3 Treatment Duration**

Treatment will continue until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal of consent, or completion of 12 cycles of chemotherapy, whichever occurs first. Subjects who complete 12 cycles of chemotherapy and derive clinical benefit per investigator assessment may receive MOC-221 monotherapy until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

**6. STUDY PROCEDURES**
**6.2 Efficacy Assessments**

**6.3 Safety Assessments**

Adverse events will be graded according to NCI CTCAE version 5.0. All adverse events will be recorded from the time of informed consent through 30 days after the last dose of study treatment, or until initiation of a new anti-cancer therapy, whichever occurs first. Serious adverse events will be recorded from the time of informed consent through 30 days after the last dose of study treatment, or 90 days after the last dose if the event is considered related to study treatment.

**6.4 Laboratory Assessments**

All laboratory samples will be processed at the central laboratory (LabCorp Singapore). Local laboratory results may be used for urgent clinical management, but central laboratory results will be used for all protocol decisions including dose modifications. Samples collected at unscheduled visits must be processed through the central laboratory whenever feasible.

**7. STATISTICAL CONSIDERATIONS**

The sample size of 80 subjects provides approximately 85% power to detect a difference in progression-free survival between the treatment groups, assuming a hazard ratio of 0.65, using a two-sided log-rank test at a significance level of 0.05.

**7.2 Analysis Populations**

- **Intent-to-Treat (ITT) Population:** All subjects who are randomized.
- **Safety Population:** All subjects who receive at least one dose of any study treatment.
- **Per-Protocol Population:** All subjects in the ITT population who complete the study without major protocol deviations.

MOC-221 has a serious adverse event count of 2 events. Record status: current.

**7.3 Primary Analysis**

The primary endpoint of progression-free survival will be compared between treatment arms using a stratified log-rank test. A stratified Cox proportional hazards model will be used to estimate the hazard ratio and corresponding 95% confidence interval.

**7.4 Interim Analysis**

One interim analysis for futility is planned after approximately 50% of expected progression-free survival events have been observed. The interim analysis will be performed by an independent data monitoring committee. No formal alpha spending is planned for the interim analysis; the study will not stop early for efficacy.

**8. ADVERSE EVENT REPORTING**

An adverse event (AE) is any untoward medical occurrence in a subject administered a study treatment, which does not necessarily have a causal relationship with the treatment. A serious adverse event (SAE) is defined as any untoward medical occurrence that:

- Results in death,
- Is life-threatening,
- Requires inpatient hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization,
- Results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity,
- Is a congenital anomaly/birth defect,
- Or is an important medical event that may jeopardize the subject or may require medical or surgical intervention to prevent one of the outcomes listed above.

**8.2 Reporting Requirements**

All SAEs must be reported to the sponsor within 24 hours of the site becoming aware of the event, using the Serious Adverse Event Report Form. The investigator must provide follow-up information within 5 calendar days of the initial report. The sponsor is responsible for reporting SAEs to the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) and to the relevant ethics committee in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.

**8.3 Pregnancy Reporting**

Pregnancies occurring in female subjects or partners of male subjects during the study or within 6 months after the last dose of study treatment must be reported to the sponsor within 24 hours of site awareness. Pregnancies will be followed until completion or termination.
MOC-221 is a selective small-molecule inhibitor of mutant BRAF V600E and V600K kinases. Preclinical studies demonstrated potent inhibition of the MAPK pathway in BRAF-mutant melanoma cell lines and tumor xenografts. The clinical development program has established a manageable safety profile and encouraging antitumor activity in the metastatic setting. This study evaluates whether adjuvant treatment with MOC-221 improves outcomes in subjects with resected high-risk melanoma.

**2. STUDY OBJECTIVES**

**2.1 Primary Objective**

To evaluate whether adjuvant treatment with MOC-221, compared with placebo, prolongs recurrence-free survival (RFS) in subjects with completely resected Stage IIB–IIIC melanoma.

**2.2 Secondary Objectives**

- To evaluate overall survival (OS)
- To evaluate distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS)
- To assess the safety and tolerability of MOC-221
- To evaluate health-related quality of life (HRQoL)

**3. STUDY DESIGN**

This is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 study. Approximately 300 subjects will be randomized in a 2:1 ratio to receive MOC-221 or matching placebo.

Subjects will be stratified by disease stage (IIB vs. IIC vs. IIIA vs. IIIB vs. IIIC) and BRAF mutation status (V600E vs. V600K).

**4. SUBJECT POPULATION**

**4.1 Inclusion Criteria**

Subjects must meet all of the following criteria to be enrolled:

The Health Sciences Authority (HSA) has approved trial MOC-221. Record status: current.

1. Histologically confirmed diagnosis of cutaneous melanoma Stage IIB, IIC, IIIA, IIIB, or IIIC (per AJCC 8th edition).
2. Complete surgical resection of all disease within 12 weeks prior to randomization, with negative margins documented by pathology.
3. Documented BRAF V600E or V600K mutation in the tumor tissue.
4. Age ≥ 18 years.
5. ECOG performance status 0 or 1.
6. Adequate organ function as defined in Section 5.1.
7. Negative serum pregnancy test within 72 hours prior to first dose for women of childbearing potential.

**4.2 Exclusion Criteria**

Subjects meeting any of the following criteria are not eligible:

1. Prior systemic therapy for melanoma (excluding adjuvant interferon or PD-1 inhibitor completed more than 6 months prior to diagnosis of current disease).
2. Prior radiation therapy to the site of the primary lesion or regional nodes.
3. Known hypersensitivity to any component of MOC-221.
4. History of another malignancy within 2 years, except for adequately treated basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma of the skin, or carcinoma in situ of the cervix.
5. Active infection requiring systemic therapy.
6. Known history of HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C infection.
7. Uncontrolled intercurrent illness including, but not limited to, symptomatic congestive heart failure, unstable angina, or cardiac arrhythmia.
8. Pregnant or breastfeeding.

**5. STUDY TREATMENT**

**5.1 Dosing Schedule**

MOC-221 will be administered orally at a dose of 150 mg twice daily (BID), continuously in 28-day cycles. Treatment will continue until disease recurrence, unacceptable toxicity, or completion of 12 cycles, whichever occurs first.

Subjects with moderate renal impairment (creatinine clearance 30–59 mL/min) will receive a reduced dose of 100 mg BID. Subjects with severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance < 30 mL/min) will receive 75 mg BID.

**5.2 Dose Modifications**

Dose modifications for treatment-related toxicities are detailed in Appendix B. In general, adverse events of Grade 3 or higher will require dose interruption until resolution to Grade 1 or baseline, followed by dose reduction by one level. A maximum of two dose reductions is permitted.

**6. STUDY PROCEDURES**
**PROTOCOL MOC-221**

**A Phase 2, Multicenter, Open-Label Study of MOC-221 (Oral BRAF Inhibitor) in Subjects with Unresectable or Metastatic Melanoma Harboring BRAF V600E or V600K Mutations**

**Sponsor:** NovoPharm Clinical Pte. Ltd.

**Protocol Version History**

| Version | Effective Date | Amendment Summary |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | 15 Jan 2022 | Original protocol. |
| 2.0 | 03 May 2022 | Amendment 1: Clarified exclusion criterion for prior PD-1 inhibitor therapy; added moderate renal impairment dosing. |
| 3.0 | 12 Sep 2022 | Amendment 2: Updated Appendix B toxicity management table; added Singapore-specific adverse event reporting timelines. |
| 3.1 | 05 Dec 2022 | Administrative change: Updated contact details for the Singapore coordinating center. |
| 4.0 | 20 Mar 2023 | Amendment 3: Extended treatment duration from 12 to 18 cycles for subjects with confirmed partial response or better at Cycle 12. |

**7. WITHDRAWAL OF SUBJECTS**

**7.1 Withdrawal Criteria**

A subject may be withdrawn from study treatment for any of the following reasons:

1. Disease recurrence or progression as defined by RECIST 1.1.
2. Unacceptable toxicity as defined in Section 5.2.
3. Subject request to discontinue treatment.
4. Investigator discretion.
5. Protocol deviation requiring withdrawal as determined by the Sponsor.

Subjects who discontinue study treatment will continue to be followed for survival and subsequent therapies, unless they withdraw consent for all follow-up.

**7.2 Replacement of Subjects**

Subjects who withdraw from the study prior to completing Cycle 1 will be replaced. Replacement subjects will be assigned the next available subject number.

**8. STUDY ASSESSMENTS AND PROCEDURES (CONTINUED)**

**8.1 Tumor Response Assessment**

Tumor response will be assessed using RECIST 1.1 criteria. Computed tomography (CT) scans of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis will be performed at baseline, then every 8 weeks (± 1 week) for the first 12 months, and every 12 weeks thereafter. Subjects with known or suspected brain metastases will undergo magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain at the same intervals.

Responses will be confirmed by repeat imaging no less than 4 weeks after the initial observation of response.

**8.2 Safety Assessments**

Safety will be assessed throughout the study via:

- Physical examinations
- Vital signs
- Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status
- Laboratory evaluations (hematology, serum chemistry, liver function tests, renal function)
- Electrocardiograms (ECGs) at baseline, Day 1 of each cycle, and at end of treatment
- Adverse event (AE) monitoring from the time of informed consent through 30 days after the last dose of study treatment

**8.3 Pharmacokinetic Sampling**

Blood samples for pharmacokinetic (PK) analysis will be collected at the following time points:

- Cycle 1 Day 1: pre-dose, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, and 12 hours post-dose
- Cycle 1 Day 15: pre-dose
- Cycle 2 Day 1: pre-dose
- Cycle 4 Day 1: pre-dose

PK samples will be analyzed for MOC-221 and its primary metabolite, MOC-221-M1. Results will be reported in a separate PK analysis report.

**9. STATISTICAL CONSIDERATIONS**

**9.1 Study Endpoints**

**9.1.1 Primary Endpoint**

The primary endpoint is overall response rate (ORR), defined as the proportion of subjects achieving a confirmed best overall response of complete response (CR) or partial response (PR) as determined by investigator assessment using RECIST 1.1.
**10. STATISTICAL CONSIDERATIONS (CONTINUED)**

**10.2 Analysis Sets**

The Full Analysis Set (FAS) will include all subjects who receive at least one dose of study treatment. The Per-Protocol Set (PPS) will include all subjects in the FAS who complete Cycle 1 without major protocol deviations. The Safety Analysis Set will include all subjects who receive at least one dose of study treatment.

**10.3 Sample Size and Power**

A total of 120 subjects will be enrolled. This sample size provides approximately 80% power to detect an improvement in ORR from a historical control of 20% to an assumed ORR of 35%, using a two-sided exact binomial test at a significance level of 0.05.

**10.4 Primary Analysis**

The primary analysis of ORR will be performed when all subjects have completed at least 6 cycles of treatment or have discontinued earlier. The point estimate and 95% exact confidence interval will be presented. Subjects with missing response assessments will be considered non-responders in the primary analysis.

**10.5 Secondary Analyses**

Secondary endpoints will be analyzed descriptively. Time-to-event endpoints (progression-free survival, duration of response, overall survival) will be summarized using Kaplan-Meier methods. Subgroup analyses will be performed by age, sex, ECOG performance status, and prior lines of therapy.

**10.6 Interim Analysis**

An interim analysis for futility will be conducted after 60 subjects have been evaluated for response. The study will be stopped early for futility if the observed ORR is less than 15%. No alpha adjustment is required as the interim analysis is for futility only.

**10.7 Handling of Missing Data**

No imputation will be performed for the primary endpoint. For safety analyses, missing laboratory values will not be imputed. For time-to-event endpoints, subjects without an event will be censored at the date of last known follow-up.

**11. ADMINISTRATIVE REQUIREMENTS**

**11.1 Regulatory and Ethical Considerations**

The study will be conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki, the International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and applicable local regulations. Prior to study initiation, the protocol, informed consent form, and any other subject-facing materials will be submitted to the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) and the relevant Institutional Review Board (IRB) for review and approval.

**11.2 Informed Consent**

Written informed consent will be obtained from each subject prior to any study-specific procedures. The informed consent form will describe the purpose of the study, the procedures involved, potential risks and benefits, and the subject's rights. Subjects will be given ample time to consider their participation and will be encouraged to discuss the study with their family, friends, or primary physician.

**11.3 Subject Confidentiality**

All subject data will be handled in accordance with the Singapore Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA). Subject identifiers will be coded, and a subject identification log linking codes to personal data will be maintained securely at the investigational site. Study data will be stored in a locked cabinet and on password-protected computers.

**11.4 Protocol Amendments**

Any changes to the protocol will be documented in a formal amendment. Substantial amendments will be submitted to the IRB and HSA for approval prior to implementation. Nonsubstantial amendments will be submitted for information purposes. A summary of all amendments is provided in the table below.
**12. REFERENCES**

1. International Council for Harmonisation (ICH). Guideline for Good Clinical Practice E6(R2). Current step 4 version, dated 9 November 2016.
2. World Medical Association. Declaration of Helsinki – Ethical Principles for Medical Research Involving Human Subjects. Latest revision, October 2013 (Fortaleza, Brazil).
3. Singapore Personal Data Protection Act 2012 (No. 26 of 2012), as amended.
4. Health Sciences Authority. Guidance on Clinical Trial Submission for Medicinal Products in Singapore. Version 2.1, dated 1 April 2021.
5. NovoPharm Clinical. MOC-221 Investigational Medicinal Product Dossier. Version 3.0, dated 12 January 2023.
6. NovoPharm Clinical. Central Laboratory Manual for MOC-221. Version 1.2, dated 3 March 2023.
7. European Medicines Agency. ICH E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials. CPMP/ICH/363/96, September 1998.

**13. APPENDICES**

**Appendix A: Schedule of Assessments**

The detailed Schedule of Assessments is provided as a separate document (MOC-221-SoA, Version 2.1, dated 15 February 2023). The schedule is binding for all sites. Any deviation must be documented and reported to the Medical Monitor. A summary of key visit windows for the treatment period is included below for reference.

**Appendix B: Laboratory Reference Ranges**

The central laboratory will provide a full listing of reference ranges for all parameters collected. Site laboratories may be used for routine safety monitoring where permitted by the local health authority, provided that the laboratory holds relevant accreditation and the reference ranges are submitted to the sponsor prior to study initiation. A sample of critical ranges for haematology parameters is provided below for planning purposes only; these do not supersede the central laboratory values.

**Appendix C: Concomitant Medication Coding**

Concomitant medications will be coded using the most current version of the World Health Organization Drug Dictionary (WHO DD). The version used for coding will be recorded in the clinical study report. Medications will be classified according to the Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification system.

**Appendix D: Adverse Event Severity Grading**

Adverse events will be graded according to the National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (NCI CTCAE), Version 5.0. documents.title: Protocol MOC-221 and Amendments
documents.content:
This document is confidential and contains proprietary information belonging to NovoPharm Clinical. It may not be used, disclosed, or reproduced without prior written consent. The current version in use at all participating sites is Protocol MOC-221-Rev3.

1. BACKGROUND AND RATIONALE

Pancreatic adenocarcinoma remains a disease with significant unmet medical need. Despite advances in systemic therapy, the five-year survival rate for subjects with locally advanced or metastatic disease remains below 10%. The standard of care, gemcitabine-based regimens, offers modest survival benefit but is associated with substantial toxicity. There is therefore a pressing need for novel therapeutic approaches that can improve outcomes without unacceptable adverse effects.

MOC-221 is a selective small molecule inhibitor targeting the MAPK signalling pathway downstream of KRAS mutations. Preclinical studies demonstrated synergistic anti-tumour activity when MOC-221 was combined with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel in xenograft models. The current Phase II study is designed to evaluate this combination in a larger cohort of subjects with pancreatic adenocarcinoma who have not received prior systemic therapy for advanced disease.

2. STUDY OBJECTIVES

2.1 Primary Objective

To evaluate the anti-tumour activity of MOC-221 in combination with standard-of-care chemotherapy as measured by progression-free survival (PFS) per RECIST v1.1 as assessed by investigator review.

2.2 Secondary Objectives

- To characterise the safety and tolerability profile of MOC-221 when administered with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel
- To estimate overall survival (OS)
- To evaluate objective response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DoR)
- To assess pharmacokinetic parameters of MOC-221 when given in combination
- To evaluate changes in quality of life using the EORTC QLQ-C30 instrument

MOC-221 protocol_version_in_use Protocol MOC-221-Rev3. Record status: current.

2.3 Exploratory Objectives

- To investigate the relationship between tumour KRAS mutation status and clinical activity
- To evaluate potential predictive biomarkers in archival tumour tissue
- To assess immunogenicity of MOC-221

3. STUDY DESIGN

This is a Phase II, open-label, single-arm, multi-centre study. A total of approximately 75 subjects will be enrolled across approximately 15 sites in Asia-Pacific, including Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, and Australia.

Subjects will receive MOC-221 at a dose of 300 mg orally twice daily continuously in 28-day cycles. In addition, subjects will receive gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² intravenously on Days 1, 8, and 15 of each cycle and nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m² intravenously on Days 1, 8, and 15 of each cycle.

Treatment will continue until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal of consent, or a maximum of 12 cycles of chemotherapy, whichever occurs first. Subjects who complete 12 cycles of chemotherapy and derive clinical benefit may receive MOC-221 monotherapy until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

The study will utilise a Simon two-stage design. An interim analysis will be conducted after the first 25 subjects have been followed for at least 16 weeks. If fewer than 8 subjects are progression-free at that timepoint, enrolment will be halted for futility. Otherwise, the study will continue to full enrolment.

4. SUBJECT SELECTION

4.1 Inclusion Criteria

Subjects must satisfy all of the following criteria to be eligible for the study:

4.1.5 Subjects must have adequate haematological, hepatic, and renal function as defined below:
- Absolute neutrophil count ≥ 1.5 × 10⁹/L
- Haemoglobin ≥ 9.0 g/dL
- Platelet count ≥ 100 × 10⁹/L
- Total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 × upper limit of normal (ULN)
- AST and ALT ≤ 3.0 × ULN (≤ 5.0 × ULN if liver metastases are present)
- Serum creatinine ≤ 1.5 × ULN or calculated creatinine clearance ≥ 50 mL/min

4.1.6 Subjects must have an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 or 1.

4.1.7 Subjects must have archival tumour tissue available for KRAS mutation status testing, or consent to a fresh biopsy at screening.

4.1.8 Subjects must be willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests, and other study procedures.

**4.2 Exclusion Criteria**

Subjects who meet any of the following criteria are not eligible for the study:

4.2.1 Prior systemic therapy for metastatic PDAC. Prior adjuvant therapy is permitted if completed at least 6 months prior to diagnosis of metastatic disease.

4.2.2 Known active central nervous system metastases.

4.2.3 Clinically significant cardiovascular disease, including myocardial infarction within 6 months, unstable angina, New York Heart Association Class III or IV congestive heart failure, or QTc interval > 470 ms on screening ECG.

4.2.4 Known history of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection, active hepatitis B or hepatitis C infection.

4.2.5 Major surgical procedure within 28 days prior to first dose of study treatment.

4.2.6 Known hypersensitivity to any component of MOC-221, gemcitabine, or nab-paclitaxel.

4.2.7 Pregnant or breastfeeding women. Women of childbearing potential must have a negative serum pregnancy test at screening and agree to use highly effective contraception during the study and for 6 months after the last dose of study treatment.

The enrollment target for MOC-221 is 80 patients. Record status: current.

4.2.8 Any other condition that, in the opinion of the investigator, would compromise the safety of the subject or interfere with the interpretation of study results.

**5. STUDY TREATMENT**

**5.1 Dosing Schedule**

Subjects will receive the following treatment regimens in 28-day cycles:

| Drug | Dose | Route | Schedule |
|------|------|-------|----------|
| MOC-221 | 300 mg | Oral | Twice daily, Days 1–28 continuously |
| Gemcitabine | 1000 mg/m² | IV | Days 1, 8, 15 |
| Nab-paclitaxel | 125 mg/m² | IV | Days 1, 8, 15 |

MOC-221 should be taken with food at approximately the same time each morning and evening. If a dose is missed, the subject should not make up the dose; the next scheduled dose should be taken at the regular time.

**5.2 Dose Modifications**

Dose modifications for gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel will follow standard guidelines for haematological and non-haematological toxicities. MOC-221 dose modifications are as follows:

- Grade 2 non-haematological toxicity (excluding alopecia): hold MOC-221 until resolution to ≤ Grade 1, then resume at same dose.
- Grade 3 non-haematological toxicity: hold MOC-221 until resolution to ≤ Grade 1, then resume at reduced dose of 200 mg twice daily.
- Grade 4 toxicity: discontinue MOC-221 permanently.

**5.3 Treatment Duration**

Treatment will continue until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal of consent, or completion of 12 cycles of chemotherapy, whichever occurs first. Subjects who complete 12 cycles of chemotherapy and derive clinical benefit per investigator assessment may receive MOC-221 monotherapy until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

**6. STUDY PROCEDURES**

**6.2 Efficacy Assessments**

**6.3 Safety Assessments**

Adverse events will be graded according to NCI CTCAE version 5.0. All adverse events will be recorded from the time of informed consent through 30 days after the last dose of study treatment, or until initiation of a new anti-cancer therapy, whichever occurs first. Serious adverse events will be recorded from the time of informed consent through 30 days after the last dose of study treatment, or 90 days after the last dose if the event is considered related to study treatment.

**6.4 Laboratory Assessments**

All laboratory samples will be processed at the central laboratory (LabCorp Singapore). Local laboratory results may be used for urgent clinical management, but central laboratory results will be used for all protocol decisions including dose modifications. Samples collected at unscheduled visits must be processed through the central laboratory whenever feasible.

**7. STATISTICAL CONSIDERATIONS**

The sample size of 80 subjects provides approximately 85% power to detect a difference in progression-free survival between the treatment groups, assuming a hazard ratio of 0.65, using a two-sided log-rank test at a significance level of 0.05.

**7.2 Analysis Populations**

- **Intent-to-Treat (ITT) Population:** All subjects who are randomized.
- **Safety Population:** All subjects who receive at least one dose of any study treatment.
- **Per-Protocol Population:** All subjects in the ITT population who complete the study without major protocol deviations.

MOC-221 has a serious adverse event count of 2 events. Record status: current.

**7.3 Primary Analysis**

The primary endpoint of progression-free survival will be compared between treatment arms using a stratified log-rank test. A stratified Cox proportional hazards model will be used to estimate the hazard ratio and corresponding 95% confidence interval.

**7.4 Interim Analysis**

One interim analysis for futility is planned after approximately 50% of expected progression-free survival events have been observed. The interim analysis will be performed by an independent data monitoring committee. No formal alpha spending is planned for the interim analysis; the study will not stop early for efficacy.

**8. ADVERSE EVENT REPORTING**

An adverse event (AE) is any untoward medical occurrence in a subject administered a study treatment, which does not necessarily have a causal relationship with the treatment. A serious adverse event (SAE) is defined as any untoward medical occurrence that:

- Results in death,
- Is life-threatening,
- Requires inpatient hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization,
- Results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity,
- Is a congenital anomaly/birth defect,
- Or is an important medical event that may jeopardize the subject or may require medical or surgical intervention to prevent one of the outcomes listed above.

**8.2 Reporting Requirements**

All SAEs must be reported to the sponsor within 24 hours of the site becoming aware of the event, using the Serious Adverse Event Report Form. The investigator must provide follow-up information within 5 calendar days of the initial report. The sponsor is responsible for reporting SAEs to the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) and to the relevant ethics committee in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.

**8.3 Pregnancy Reporting**

Pregnancies occurring in female subjects or partners of male subjects during the study or within 6 months after the last dose of study treatment must be reported to the sponsor within 24 hours of site awareness. Pregnancies will be followed until completion or termination.

documents.content:
MOC-221 is a selective small-molecule inhibitor of mutant BRAF V600E and V600K kinases. Preclinical studies demonstrated potent inhibition of the MAPK pathway in BRAF-mutant melanoma cell lines and tumor xenografts. The clinical development program has established a manageable safety profile and encouraging antitumor activity in the metastatic setting. This study evaluates whether adjuvant treatment with MOC-221 improves outcomes in subjects with resected high-risk melanoma.

**2. STUDY OBJECTIVES**

**2.1 Primary Objective**

To evaluate whether adjuvant treatment with MOC-221, compared with placebo, prolongs recurrence-free survival (RFS) in subjects with completely resected Stage IIB–IIIC melanoma.

**2.2 Secondary Objectives**

- To evaluate overall survival (OS)
- To evaluate distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS)
- To assess the safety and tolerability of MOC-221
- To evaluate health-related quality of life (HRQoL)

**3. STUDY DESIGN**

This is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 study. Approximately 300 subjects will be randomized in a 2:1 ratio to receive MOC-221 or matching placebo.

Subjects will be stratified by disease stage (IIB vs. IIC vs. IIIA vs. IIIB vs. IIIC) and BRAF mutation status (V600E vs. V600K).

**4. SUBJECT POPULATION**

**4.1 Inclusion Criteria**

Subjects must meet all of the following criteria to be enrolled:

The Health Sciences Authority (HSA) has approved trial MOC-221. Record status: current.

1. Histologically confirmed diagnosis of cutaneous melanoma Stage IIB, IIC, IIIA, IIIB, or IIIC (per AJCC 8th edition).
2. Complete surgical resection of all disease within 12 weeks prior to randomization, with negative margins documented by pathology.
3. Documented BRAF V600E or V600K mutation in the tumor tissue.
4. Age ≥ 18 years.
5. ECOG performance status 0 or 1.
6. Adequate organ function as defined in Section 5.1.
7. Negative serum pregnancy test within 72 hours prior to first dose for women of childbearing potential.

**4.2 Exclusion Criteria**

Subjects meeting any of the following criteria are not eligible:

1. Prior systemic therapy for melanoma (excluding adjuvant interferon or PD-1 inhibitor completed more than 6 months prior to diagnosis of current disease).
2. Prior radiation therapy to the site of the primary lesion or regional nodes.
3. Known hypersensitivity to any component of MOC-221.
4. History of another malignancy within 2 years, except for adequately treated basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma of the skin, or carcinoma in situ of the cervix.
5. Active infection requiring systemic therapy.
6. Known history of HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C infection.
7. Uncontrolled intercurrent illness including, but not limited to, symptomatic congestive heart failure, unstable angina, or cardiac arrhythmia.
8. Pregnant or breastfeeding.

**5. STUDY TREATMENT**

**5.1 Dosing Schedule**

MOC-221 will be administered orally at a dose of 150 mg twice daily (BID), continuously in 28-day cycles. Treatment will continue until disease recurrence, unacceptable toxicity, or completion of 12 cycles, whichever occurs first.

Subjects with moderate renal impairment (creatinine clearance 30–59 mL/min) will receive a reduced dose of 100 mg BID. Subjects with severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance < 30 mL/min) will receive 75 mg BID.

**5.2 Dose Modifications**

Dose modifications for treatment-related toxicities are detailed in Appendix B. In general, adverse events of Grade 3 or higher will require dose interruption until resolution to Grade 1 or baseline, followed by dose reduction by one level. A maximum of two dose reductions is permitted.

**6. STUDY PROCEDURES**

**7. WITHDRAWAL OF SUBJECTS**

**7.1 Withdrawal Criteria**

A subject may be withdrawn from study treatment for any of the following reasons:

1. Disease recurrence or progression as defined by RECIST 1.1.
2. Unacceptable toxicity as defined in Section 5.2.
3. Subject request to discontinue treatment.
4. Investigator discretion.
5. Protocol deviation requiring withdrawal as determined by the Sponsor.

Subjects who discontinue study treatment will continue to be followed for survival and subsequent therapies, unless they withdraw consent for all follow-up.

**7.2 Replacement of Subjects**

Subjects who withdraw from the study prior to completing Cycle 1 will be replaced. Replacement subjects will be assigned the next available subject number.

**8. STUDY ASSESSMENTS AND PROCEDURES (CONTINUED)**

**8.1 Tumor Response Assessment**

Tumor response will be assessed using RECIST 1.1 criteria. Computed tomography (CT) scans of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis will be performed at baseline, then every 8 weeks (± 1 week) for the first 12 months, and every 12 weeks thereafter. Subjects with known or suspected brain metastases will undergo magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain at the same intervals.

Responses will be confirmed by repeat imaging no less than 4 weeks after the initial observation of response.

**8.2 Safety Assessments**

Safety will be assessed throughout the study via:

- Physical examinations
- Vital signs
- Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status
- Laboratory evaluations (hematology, serum chemistry, liver function tests, renal function)
- Electrocardiograms (ECGs) at baseline, Day 1 of each cycle, and at end of treatment
- Adverse event (AE) monitoring from the time of informed consent through 30 days after the last dose of study treatment

**8.3 Pharmacokinetic Sampling**

Blood samples for pharmacokinetic (PK) analysis will be collected at the following time points:

- Cycle 1 Day 1: pre-dose, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, and 12 hours post-dose
- Cycle 1 Day 15: pre-dose
- Cycle 2 Day 1: pre-dose
- Cycle 4 Day 1: pre-dose

PK samples will be analyzed for MOC-221 and its primary metabolite, MOC-221-M1. Results will be reported in a separate PK analysis report.

**9. STATISTICAL CONSIDERATIONS**

**9.1 Study Endpoints**

**9.1.1 Primary Endpoint**

The primary endpoint is overall response rate (ORR), defined as the proportion of subjects achieving a confirmed best overall response of complete response (CR) or partial response (PR) as determined by investigator assessment using RECIST 1.1.

**10. STATISTICAL CONSIDERATIONS (CONTINUED)**

**10.2 Analysis Sets**

The Full Analysis Set (FAS) will include all subjects who receive at least one dose of study treatment. The Per-Protocol Set (PPS) will include all subjects in the FAS who complete Cycle 1 without major protocol deviations. The Safety Analysis Set will include all subjects who receive at least one dose of study treatment.

**10.3 Sample Size and Power**

A total of 120 subjects will be enrolled. This sample size provides approximately 80% power to detect an improvement in ORR from a historical control of 20% to an assumed ORR of 35%, using a two-sided exact binomial test at a significance level of 0.05.

**10.4 Primary Analysis**

The primary analysis of ORR will be performed when all subjects have completed at least 6 cycles of treatment or have discontinued earlier. The point estimate and 95% exact confidence interval will be presented. Subjects with missing response assessments will be considered non-responders in the primary analysis.

**10.5 Secondary Analyses**

Secondary endpoints will be analyzed descriptively. Time-to-event endpoints (progression-free survival, duration of response, overall survival) will be summarized using Kaplan-Meier methods. Subgroup analyses will be performed by age, sex, ECOG performance status, and prior lines of therapy.

**10.6 Interim Analysis**

An interim analysis for futility will be conducted after 60 subjects have been evaluated for response. The study will be stopped early for futility if the observed ORR is less than 15%. No alpha adjustment is required as the interim analysis is for futility only.

**10.7 Handling of Missing Data**

No imputation will be performed for the primary endpoint. For safety analyses, missing laboratory values will not be imputed. For time-to-event endpoints, subjects without an event will be censored at the date of last known follow-up.

**11. ADMINISTRATIVE REQUIREMENTS**

**11.1 Regulatory and Ethical Considerations**

The study will be conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki, the International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and applicable local regulations. Prior to study initiation, the protocol, informed consent form, and any other subject-facing materials will be submitted to the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) and the relevant Institutional Review Board (IRB) for review and approval.

**11.2 Informed Consent**

Written informed consent will be obtained from each subject prior to any study-specific procedures. The informed consent form will describe the purpose of the study, the procedures involved, potential risks and benefits, and the subject's rights. Subjects will be given ample time to consider their participation and will be encouraged to discuss the study with their family, friends, or primary physician.

**11.3 Subject Confidentiality**

All subject data will be handled in accordance with the Singapore Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA). Subject identifiers will be coded, and a subject identification log linking codes to personal data will be maintained securely at the investigational site. Study data will be stored in a locked cabinet and on password-protected computers.

**11.4 Protocol Amendments**

Any changes to the protocol will be documented in a formal amendment. Substantial amendments will be submitted to the IRB and HSA for approval prior to implementation. Nonsubstantial amendments will be submitted for information purposes. A summary of all amendments is provided in the table below.
